title: The Web Browser Is All You Need - Paul Klein IV, Browserbase
talk_summary: A Browserbase founder argues that headless browsers (via a horizontal browser MCP server or the Stagehand framework) are the universal fallback integration for agents hitting the legacy web, and that web agents should be built with model-agnostic infra, own evals, and full session observability. Most of the talk is product positioning; the transferable mechanisms are the agent-vs-tool distinction, accessibility-tree context reduction, per-task model evals, and session recording.

takeaways.technique: Browser as fallback integration (horizontal tool) instead of per-service MCPs
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a small set of generic primitives (navigate, click, type) that work on any site, rather than building a bespoke integration per service; use vertical MCPs only where a first-party API exists.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a browser is kind of the integration of last resort, the path that you can take your agent down if you don't have something

takeaways.technique: Accessibility-tree context instead of raw HTML
takeaways.what_they_do: For DOM-based agents, transform page HTML into the accessibility tree to strip divs/classes and condense the same layout into far fewer tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the accessibility tree ... you can take a different structure of the same information and condense it down

takeaways.technique: Own task-specific model evals instead of public benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: Run private evals per task/site to pick which model is actually best, rather than trusting vendor-published benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most benchmarks are fake news ... You really need your own evals

takeaways.technique: Distinguish deterministic browser tools from autonomous web agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Use single-action tools ('click sign-in') when the workflow is known and repeatable; reserve free-roaming agents ('one prompt to many actions') for unknown paths, because agents are non-deterministic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a web agent is kind of like one prompt to many actions ... browser tools are like one action or one prompt

takeaways.technique: Session recording and action logs for agent observability
takeaways.what_they_do: Record every browser session (screenshots, action history, page paths) so failures like 'bought AirPods instead of an Xbox' can be traced to prompts and steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: taking screenshots, recording history, recording actions, making sure that you know exactly where your agent went to and why

takeaways.technique: Be a good citizen / rate-limit outbound agent behavior
takeaways.what_they_do: Advise obeying robots.txt and per-site rate limits because behavioral detection blocks agents that act too aggressively, regardless of stealth.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to be a good citizen of the internet first. You need to try and obey robots.ext
